fixes.explanation: The verse never mentions enemies watching. The reason it gives is right there in the same sentence: “Do not be arrogant, for the LORD has spoken.” (Jeremiah 13:15) The reason is that the LORD has spoken, and nobody else's opinion is part of it.

It's actually true. Jeremiah 13:16 says, “You wait for light, but He turns it into deep gloom and thick darkness.” In that same verse, the people are told to give glory to the LORD their God before He brings darkness. So the statement says just what the verse says.

The verse says nothing about the king turning the city against Jeremiah. The tears come “…because the LORD’s flock has been taken captive.” (Jeremiah 13:17) That's the reason the verse gives, and it's the only one.

Golden isn't the word in the text. The verse says, “Take a lowly seat, for your glorious crowns have fallen from your heads.” (Jeremiah 13:18) The crowns are called glorious, and the seat is called lowly.
The text doesn't send anyone from the east. It says, “Lift up your eyes and see those coming from the north.” (Jeremiah 13:20) The direction is stated plainly, so north is the one to remember.
Labor is right. The verse asks, “Will not pangs of anguish grip you, as they do a woman in labor?” (Jeremiah 13:21) It's a picture of anguish that grips them. It shows how deep the anguish will be.
Court doesn't fit here. The verse says the anguish grips them “…as they do a woman in labor?” (Jeremiah 13:21) The comparison is to a woman in labor, not to a trial.

Battle is a fair guess, but the verse says labor. It asks, “Will not pangs of anguish grip you, as they do a woman in labor?” (Jeremiah 13:21) The comparison is anguish that grips, like a woman in labor.

False is right. The text says, “It is because of the magnitude of your iniquity that your skirts have been stripped off and your body has been exposed.” (Jeremiah 13:22) It doesn't say anything about enemies being too strong. It gives what to answer if they ask, “Why has this happened to me?”
